newsitem.title: USA: Hewlett to revamp medical products unit.
newsitem.headline: Hewlett to revamp medical products unit.

text.p: Hewlett-Packard Co said Tuesday it will restructure its Medical Products Group, consolidating product lines, disbanding groups and cutting staff.

Overall, the company said 250 jobs would be cut in the restructuring. It expects the costs of restructuring to be incurred in the first and second quarters of 1997, but those costs "will not be materially significant," it said.
The company will consolidate its heart defibrillator and electrocardiograph product lines in McMinnville, Ore., into its Resuscitation Division in Andover, Mass.
Of the 152 employees effected, 100 will be offered new jobs in the Resuscitation Division. The transition will take 90 to 120 days, Hewlett-Packard said.
HP's Healthcare Information Management Division in Andover will be disbanded, and most of its products and services will be transferred to other Medical Products Group divisions.
HP's CareVue clinical-information systems will be merged into HP's Patient Monitoring Division.

"We believe the best way to meet our customers' needs and deliver a reasonable return to shareholders is to consolidate and focus our operations in our areas of strength in clinical measurements and computation," Cynthia Danaher, general manager of Medical Products Group, said in a statement.
